syllabus_version.title: CBSE Curriculum for the Academic Year 2026-27

topics.title: A Bottle of Dew: the story and its events
topics.ncert_sections: A Bottle of Dew: Let us read I and II

concepts.learning_objective: Recall the main events of 'A Bottle of Dew' and put them in the correct order.
Explain what sage Mahipati asked Rama Natha to do and the real purpose behind the task.

topics.title: A Bottle of Dew: characters and message
topics.ncert_sections: A Bottle of Dew: Let us read II; Let us think and reflect

concepts.learning_objective: State the message of the story that wealth is created by hard work, not by magic.
Describe the qualities of Rama Natha, Madhumati and sage Mahipati from what they say and do.

topics.title: A Bottle of Dew: words, homophones and connecting words
topics.ncert_sections: A Bottle of Dew: Let us learn

concepts.learning_objective: Give the meanings of words and phrases from the story such as tended, give up and precious.
Identify homophones such as dew-due and son-sun and use them correctly in sentences.
Join ideas with suitable connecting words such as because, before and as soon as.

topics.title: The Raven and the Fox: the poem and its lesson
topics.ncert_sections: The Raven and the Fox: Let us read; Let us think and reflect

concepts.learning_objective: Recall the characters and events of the poem 'The Raven and the Fox' by Jean de La Fontaine.
Explain how the Fox used flattery and the Raven's pride, and the lesson the poem teaches.

topics.title: The Raven and the Fox: rhyme, alliteration and vocabulary
topics.ncert_sections: The Raven and the Fox: Let us learn

concepts.learning_objective: Identify rhyming words and the rhyme pattern of the stanzas of the poem.
Recognise alliteration as the repetition of the same consonant sound at the start of nearby words.
Give the meanings and opposites of words from the poem such as limb, perched and pride.

topics.title: Rama to the Rescue: the story
topics.ncert_sections: Rama to the Rescue: Let us read; Let us think and reflect

concepts.learning_objective: Recall the characters, problem and events of the story 'Rama to the Rescue'.
Explain how the couple used a clever plan and presence of mind to get help from the kotwal.

topics.title: Contractions and the present progressive tense
topics.ncert_sections: Rama to the Rescue: Let us learn I-IV

concepts.learning_objective: Expand contracted words such as they're, I'm and won't and explain the use of the apostrophe.
Form and use the present progressive tense (am/is/are + verb + ing) for actions happening now.

topics.title: Adverbs, exclamatory and interrogative sentences
topics.ncert_sections: Rama to the Rescue: Let us learn VI-X

concepts.learning_objective: Identify adverbs that tell how an action is done and choose suitable adverbs for sentences.
Distinguish exclamatory and interrogative sentences and punctuate them correctly.

topics.title: The Unlikely Best Friends (Part I): Gajaraj meets Buntee
topics.ncert_sections: Story: The Unlikely Best Friends, Part I

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why Gajaraj was sad in spite of royal comforts and how a caretaker differs from a friend.
Describe how the friendship between Gajaraj and the stray dog began and grew.
Infer the meanings of words such as 'strayed', 'accompanied' and 'yelped' from the story.

topics.title: The Unlikely Best Friends (Part II): separation and reunion
topics.ncert_sections: Story: The Unlikely Best Friends, Part II

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how Gajaraj and Buntee showed that they missed each other after being separated.
Describe how the farmer's kindness reunited the friends and created a new friendship.
Evaluate what makes the friendship of Gajaraj and Buntee 'unlikely'.

topics.title: Language from 'The Unlikely Best Friends': opposites, past tense and neither-nor
topics.ncert_sections: Let us learn (The Unlikely Best Friends)

concepts.learning_objective: Form opposites by adding prefixes such as un-, dis-, in- and mis- to words.
Distinguish the simple past, past progressive and past perfect forms of verbs.
Use 'neither ... nor' and 'either ... or' correctly to join two choices.

topics.title: A Friend's Prayer (poem)
topics.ncert_sections: Poem: A Friend's Prayer

concepts.learning_objective: Interpret the main ideas and lines of the poem 'A Friend's Prayer'.
Identify the qualities of the speaker as shown in the poem.
Understand words related to friendship such as 'blessed' and qualities of a good friend.

topics.title: The Chair: Mario and the magic chair test
topics.ncert_sections: Story: The Chair, Parts I and II

concepts.learning_objective: Recall the bet between Mario and his grandfather and describe Mario's character.
Explain how the invisible chair test worked at school.
Evaluate the story's message about who our true friends are.

topics.title: Language from 'The Chair': suffixes and adjectives
topics.ncert_sections: Let us learn (The Chair)

concepts.learning_objective: Divide words into root words and suffixes and form new words with suffixes.
Identify adjectives and pair them with suitable nouns.

topics.title: Neem Baba: the tree's origin, spread and names
topics.ncert_sections: Neem Baba, Part I; Let us explore

concepts.learning_objective: Recall where the neem tree was born and where it is found today, as told by Neem Baba.
Explain the different names of neem and the reasons behind them.

topics.title: Neem Baba: uses of neem in medicine, farming and daily life
topics.ncert_sections: Neem Baba, Part II

concepts.learning_objective: Describe how different parts of neem are used to treat illnesses and why such remedies need trained people.
Explain how neem protects crops, stored grains, homes and the air.

topics.title: Neem Baba: compound words, past forms of verbs and personification
topics.ncert_sections: Neem Baba: Let us learn I-III

concepts.learning_objective: Identify and classify open, closed and hyphenated compound words.
Match verbs showing action in the present with their past forms.
Recognise personification, where a non-human thing is given human qualities.

topics.title: What a Bird Thought: the bird's changing idea of the world
topics.ncert_sections: What a Bird Thought, poem and Let us discuss

concepts.learning_objective: Trace how the bird's idea of the world changes as it grows.
Identify the main idea of each stanza and the central message of the poem.

topics.title: What a Bird Thought: vocabulary, rhyme and describing words
topics.ncert_sections: What a Bird Thought: Let us do, Let us learn I-II

concepts.learning_objective: Understand the meaning of words like 'pale', 'fluttered', 'nestled', 'at length' and 'labours' in the poem.
Identify rhyming words and the rhyme pattern of the poem.
Identify describing words used for the bird's homes.

topics.title: Spices that Heal Us: Daadi's letter on spices
topics.ncert_sections: Spices that Heal Us, letter and Let us think and reflect

concepts.learning_objective: Recall the health benefits of common kitchen spices described in Daadi's letter.
Understand who writes the letter, why, and how home remedies pass between generations.

topics.title: Spices that Heal Us: modal verbs
topics.ncert_sections: Spices that Heal Us: Let us learn II

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the function of modals such as may, should, can, must, need to and used to.
Choose and use the right modal correctly in a sentence.

topics.title: Change of Heart: Prabhat and the Friendly Match
topics.ncert_sections: Change of Heart, Part I

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how Prabhat's fear of losing shaped the way he chose and played games.
Recall the events of the friendly badminton match and how Prabhat won it unfairly.

topics.title: Change of Heart: Surya's Attitude and Sporting Spirit
topics.ncert_sections: Change of Heart, Part II

concepts.learning_objective: Describe how Surya enjoyed games whether he won or lost.
Analyse how Prabhat changed and why sporting spirit matters.

topics.title: Change of Heart: Vocabulary, Past Perfect and Polite Expressions
topics.ncert_sections: Change of Heart: Let us learn, Let us speak

concepts.learning_objective: Give the meanings of words used in the story, such as phenomenon and opponent.
Use the past perfect tense to show which of two past actions happened first.
Choose suitable expressions with please, thank you and sorry for different situations.

topics.title: The Winner (poem by Georgia Heard)
topics.ncert_sections: The Winner

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the setting, events and meaning of the poem 'The Winner'.
Identify personification and the effect of the word pattern used in the poem.

topics.title: Yoga - A Way of Life: Meaning, Origin and Recognition
topics.ncert_sections: Yoga - A Way of Life (Let us read, Let us explore)

concepts.learning_objective: State the meaning and origin of the word yoga and the role of Sage Patanjali.
Explain how yoga has come to be recognised across the world.

topics.title: Yoga - A Way of Life: Benefits; Practice and Practise
topics.ncert_sections: Yoga - A Way of Life (Let us read, Let us learn)

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the physical and mental benefits of yoga given in the chapter.
Use the noun forms practice and advice and the verb forms practise and advise correctly.

topics.title: Hamara Bharat and the Ek Bharat, Shreshtha Bharat programme
topics.ncert_sections: Hamara Bharat - Incredible India!; Kalakritiyon ka Bharat, Part I; Let us explore 2

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how Bharat's people, culture and nature show unity in diversity and why citizens must help the country prosper.
Describe the aim of the Ek Bharat, Shreshtha Bharat programme and how state pairing builds mutual understanding.

topics.title: Folk arts and crafts of Bharat
topics.ncert_sections: Kalakritiyon ka Bharat, Part II

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the features of Aipan, the folk art of Uttarakhand.
Describe the materials and the sequence of steps used to make Dhokra metal craft.
Compare coconut shell craft of Kerala and Kondapalli toys of Andhra Pradesh.

topics.title: Sequence words, simple present tense and gakkad bharta
topics.ncert_sections: Kalakritiyon ka Bharat: Let us learn, Let us listen

concepts.learning_objective: Use sequence words such as first, next, then and finally to show the order of steps.
Use the simple present tense, adding -s/-es with he, she and it.
Recall and interpret details from Sushil's description of gakkad bharta.

topics.title: The Kites: understanding the poem
topics.ncert_sections: The Kites (poem); Let us discuss; Let us think and reflect

concepts.learning_objective: Understand what the child sees, wishes and imagines in the poem 'The Kites'.
Interpret the feelings of the child and of the people below in the poem.

topics.title: The Kites: poetic devices, kite words and the Kite Festival
topics.ncert_sections: The Kites: Let us discuss II-V; Let us learn; Let us listen

concepts.learning_objective: Identify simile, alliteration and repetition in the poem.
Name the parts of a kite and describe the structure of a cinquain poem.
Recall facts about the Kite Festival from the listening text.

topics.title: Ila Sachani: Embroidering Dreams with her Feet
topics.ncert_sections: Ila Sachani, paragraphs 1-9; Let us think and reflect

concepts.learning_objective: Describe Ila's early challenges and how her family helped her overcome them.
Explain how recognition and independence changed Ila's life and what her story teaches.

topics.title: Ila Sachani: vocabulary, words of quantity and Kathiawar embroidery
topics.ncert_sections: Ila Sachani: Let us learn I-III; Let us listen

concepts.learning_objective: Identify synonyms and antonyms of words from the lesson.
Use words of quantity correctly with countable and uncountable nouns.
Recall the features of Kathiawar embroidery from the listening text.

topics.title: National War Memorial
topics.ncert_sections: National War Memorial (poem and note)

concepts.learning_objective: Understand the purpose of the National War Memorial and the meaning of the poem about it.
